title: DARK PLACES OF THE HEART: THE HIDDEN COST OF SIN

sense.text:
“The nations of the dragons of Arabia” are the Arab world. Right now they are not coming out together. There is no unity between them; they are separate, and that is why America and Israel are able to control them over there. Some of these Arab governments are puppets for America and Israel, and some of them let America and Israel use their bases to attack Iran.

So this is not talking about right now, because he says they “shall come out with many chariots”: they are going to come together. It is a future prophecy, and it is coming. We are in the midst of it now. What is going on in the Middle East is not going to stop; with hundreds of thousands being killed in Gaza, there is no return from that.

“That all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” Right now America and Israel do not fear the Arabs, because so many of them are puppets. A time is coming when money will mean nothing to them. Right now they are controlled by the American dollar; it is going to come a time when they cannot be controlled.

The Carmanians here are Iran. He names the Arabs first, then Iran, and Iran is the old Persia, which once ruled the earth as a superpower. Don’t be fooled by the media. Fox News and the rest are a bunch of liars when they say Iran does not have enough weapons to fight. America is not going to win against Iran; Iran will give America a bloody nose. Now Israel wants to stop them from producing missiles too, and Iran is saying no.

“Raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood.” A wild boar is quiet until you keep picking at him, and once that thing goes wild, nothing can stop it. They keep killing Iran’s generals and scientists. Do you think they will stay quiet forever? That is how God described Iran.

“And with great power shall they come.” Why would God say with great power if they have no power? Who are you going to believe, men or the Bible? They are going to have certain weapons. “And join battle with them”: they will join battle with the Arabians.

“And shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” That is Israel. Every weapon Israel has, America gave it to them, and yet the scripture says Iran is going to take down a portion of it. Not with a pistol; they will have great weapons. Do not let the media fool you.

“But the end of all things is at hand.” Some do not believe it, but the Apostle Peter said it, and it is what even the white man on the news is now saying: America is done. It is not coming back. Trump cannot save it, and the talk of making America great again is propaganda. Great kingdoms last around 250 years, and this July is America’s 250th. We are in it. All we have to do is endure to the end; the kingdom is ours.

“Be ye therefore sober”: be sober in your mind. “And watch unto prayer”: watch what is going on, and pray. If you are not paying attention, the prophecy is going to skip right over your head while you watch sports. Men, try to know a little bit about everything, the law, the constitution, politics, how government works, religion, so that when someone talks to you, you do not look lost. As a leader you do not want to look stupid.

“And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves.” Above all the prophecy that is coming to pass, have fervent charity: that is the love of the brotherhood. No matter what, do not turn your back on the brotherhood. There are things coming that you cannot go through alone; that is the purpose of the brother and the sister sitting next to you. Forsake the love of the brotherhood and you are not going to make it.

If the school was shut for two weeks and you felt nothing, you are kidding yourself; you are not part of the brotherhood. The Sabbath, being around the brotherhood, is the day you should look forward to, not your job, and not staying home under the woman and the children.

“They are new every morning”: renew your spirit. The Bishop teaches prayer three times a day, morning, noon and evening. When you wake up in the morning, that is your special moment with Messiah: say shalom to your wife, the children come and say shalom to you, and you do the prayer. It is not the minute you wake up to put on the TV and see who won last night’s game.

“The Lord is my portion, saith my soul.” In this world we have nothing. The Lord is the only thing we can trust in, believe in, and have faith in. The Lord is supposed to be your portion, not your wife and not your children, and he is the one to depend on day in, day out.

“Therefore will I hope in him.” We are living in the last days and it is only going to get worse; a hundred dollars at the grocery store will not feed you for a week. Don’t pray for it to get better. Pray for it to get worse, because that is when our salvation comes. When it gets worse and worse, our hope is in the Lord.

How you know your hope is in the Lord is that you start preparing right now. The Lord is not coming from the sky with food and a house. You prepare because you believe what the scripture says, that the end is near: mentally, getting your mind right with Messiah; physically, food, shelter and a little emergency money; and spiritually, being in this day in, day out. Pray, Lord, increase my faith; Lord, help my unbelief.

This is war, and the biggest war is within yourself. Only you can keep yourself from the kingdom. The white man cannot keep you from the kingdom unless you leave this and join them. No man can take your crown if you do not allow it.

“The heart is deceitful above all things.” The heart is the mind. Nothing is more deceitful and more evil than the mind. It thinks things and you do not even know where they come from: a woman you have not dealt with in twenty years suddenly comes into your head, because you were talking to an old friend in the world who reminded you of her. That is the evil mind.

Your mind will deceive you into thinking the grass is greener on the other side, until you get there and find out you have to water it, or that it was never grass at all; it was AstroTurf.

“And desperately wicked.” Some think they are holier than thou, but the mind of every man and woman is desperately wicked. “Who can know it?” Nobody but the Most High. You can fool us, you can fool the Bishop and the leadership, but you will not fool the Most High, and you are not fooling yourself either: you know where you were last night, and why you told her to keep quiet before you answered the brother’s call.

“I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins”: only God can search the mind. “Even to give every man according to his ways”: not according to the deacon’s way or the Bishop’s way, but your way. If your way is evil, you are going to get evil; if your way is righteous, you are going to get the kingdom. You are your own biggest enemy, and there is a war going on inside you. Some will give up; some will stay until the end.

“And according to the fruit of his doings.” Most of us only see each other on the Sabbath, and when we come around each other we are on our best behavior. But there are six days of the week when we do not know where you are or what you are doing. So what are you doing when you are not here? A sister can come in for ten years bowing down, saying shalom, Most High God bless, happy Sabbath, while she is with another man. She thought she was fooling us, and she surely thought she was fooling the Most High, but you cannot fool the Most High.

precepts.why:
“All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes.” Every one of us thinks we are righteous. Ask anyone: me? I didn’t do nothing; a covetous spirit, hatred, not me. That is the deceitful heart of Jeremiah 17:9 at work.

“But the Lord weigheth the spirits.” The Lord sees everything, and you cannot hide from the Most High. He is the one who searches the heart and tries the reins, as verse 10 says.

“And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit.” The Most High searches the heart, and the heart is the mind, just as Jeremiah says, “I the Lord search the heart.”

The verse shows you have two in you: the spiritual and the physical man. There is a war, the spirit against the physical man, wicked against righteous, darkness against light, and that war will never be over until Christ comes back or you die in this. If you wonder why there is so much evil in your head, maybe it is because you are not reading enough.

And brothers, the men who do not know the scriptures are the ones who will betray you. When they come to him, he will fall, because he does not know the scriptures; the brother eating your food will plant things in your house. Young men, ask yourself honestly: the brother you talk to during the week, when is the last time the two of you talked about scripture?

sense.text:
Christ himself says how wicked the mind is: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”, evil thoughts, not righteous thoughts. Adultery is in the mind. You see your ex at the grocery store; the minute you take that phone number, before you have even said anything, that is real adultery right there. Sisters texting another man, saying I am only with him because I have nowhere to stay, all those kids should have been yours: that is an evil woman.

Fornication: we have no time for fornicators, and we will put you out. Some of you forgot the mission and what you were sent here for. The scripture says Judah shall be as God, and some do not understand the freedom and the power that comes with that; that is why they are ready to give it all for the fat stinky, something that smells like fish if it is not taken care of. Sisters too give it all away, going from a wife to a side chick to a jump-off. You curse the Son of God, you give away the kingdom of heaven, for something that smells. You should be ashamed of yourself.

Murders: hate your brother, and that is murder.

Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness. Nobody knows you more than Messiah; he created you, so he knows what is in your mind. We cannot read your mind, but Messiah God can. Some of you have an evil eye toward your brother and toward your sister.
“All these evil things come from within, and defile.” Messiah God calls everything just read evil things, and they all come from the mind. Those are the things that defile you.

precepts.why:
Some may not understand that hatred is in fact murder: “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer.” The hatred you have is equivalent to murder.

Mark 7 shows where it all begins: in your mind. Before anyone commits the act of physical murder, it has to begin with a thought, and the thought of it is the exact same thing. The hatred we have as a people one for another, God says, already makes you a murderer. You have already broken the commandment, thou shalt not kill.

sense.text:
“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light.” Christ said we are the light of the world, and you cannot be the light of the world without the scriptures. This is for the Christians who say do not keep the law: they are in darkness, because only the law can change you to become a light. Without the law you are in darkness.

“And reproofs of instruction are the way of life.” That is correction, and some cannot take correction, because correction is grievous. Correct a wife and all hell breaks loose: you were talking about pineapples, now she is talking about orange juice and bananas and things that happened two years ago.

The law keeps you grounded in life. It teaches you how to deal with your husband, your children, your brother; it is what instructs us how to live our lives. Verse 23 is a powerful scripture: counsel, counsel, counsel; prove, prove, prove. Stop doing things behind closed doors and do it the right way.

“To keep thee from the evil woman.” If you are in the law, in the scripture, it will keep you from the evil woman. But if you are evil, the law will not keep you from her: the wicked woman is given to the wicked man; that is your portion. There is nothing in secret that will not come to light. A couple that was together behind closed doors gets married, and within months the Most High puts it out. If you had taken counsel, you would have been told, that sister is not ready, that brother is not ready. Instead it comes back and bites you.

“From the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.” She tells you that you are the most handsome, and you look like Buckwheat, but you believe her, because she wants to lock you in. Some of you were set up, and now she is putting you through hell, because you were always a simp.

We leaders have nothing to gain by giving you false counsel. If a father would give a young man counsel he would not give his own son, he hates that young man, and he has no business in the position he is in.

“Lust not after her beauty in thine heart”, because beauty fades; she will not stay beautiful forever. When it fades, are you going to move on to the next one? Do not marry her for her beauty. Her beauty is supposed to start in her mind first, not on the outside. She might be beautiful but dumb as a rock; do you want that woman raising your kids?

“Neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” Brothers go out to the nations for a look, but the Bishop has always said we have every kind of sister: the Persian look, the Chinese look, the Arab look, the Indian look. You do not have to lust after another nation’s woman; no woman in this world is more beautiful than our sisters.

Sisters must get ready the way brothers get ready. Over seven hundred sisters graduated the program; if a sister drops out because she does not want to lose the weight and you marry her anyway, you are a simp who cannot control his lust. Do not marry her until she goes back to that program.

“For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread.” Some will lose the kingdom over a whorish woman. You used to be a mighty man in Israel, blessed, holding offices, traveling; then you get married and become a whole new person. The Bishop always says you do not really know a brother until he gets married. That woman turned the mighty brother into a piece of bread: soft, making excuses, bouncing after class. We know it is the woman.

“And the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.” You are that precious life. You are the prophets, the leaders of Israel, that one out of a thousand. Do not let a woman destroy that or take that away from you.

“For God shall bring every work into judgment.” No matter what you do in this life, in this body, God is going to bring it to judgment, “with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” Whatever you did in secret, good or evil, it is going to come to pass.
“Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” Nothing is hidden from him.

“Seeing then that we have a great high priest”: that is Christ, “Jesus the Son of God.” “Let us hold fast our profession.” Our profession is not our job; some hear profession and think nurse or doctor. We are prophets, and a prophet’s profession is to teach, so all of us are supposed to be teachers. Our first work is supposed to be in this truth.

What good is a prophet who does nothing with it? Some never travel and have never left the state of Georgia, yet say they are prophets. All Israel is not in Georgia; Israel is scattered to the four corners of the earth. Get a passport, brothers. We have much work to do.

“For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities.” Christ was put through the same things we are going through and worse. There is nothing you can say to him that he does not understand: the fight, the battle we face every day, the mind. None of us has an excuse. Take a break from the brotherhood because they do not understand you, and you become worse; you stay away from the one place that can help you.

Sisters, there is no such thing as a perfect sister. This place is a hospital; all of us are sick, and we come here to get healing. Christ came for those who know they are sick, not for those who say nothing is wrong with them. Stop complaining without a solution. Be patient; it takes time to get it right, and if we do not get it right we will not get the kingdom.

“But was in all points tempted”: whatever point you can think of, he was tempted, but he did not give in; “yet without sin.” Seeing your ex at the store does not mean you have to talk to them. If you say you are a follower of Christ, you are going to be tempted in all things too. Paul was tempted and did not give in. The men and women in the scriptures were just like us.

Do not let sin so overwhelm you that you lose the kingdom. We all make mistakes; when you fall, get back up. Is it so bad that you would go back to the Christian church and white Jesus, the thing you hate? And when a brother falls, it is not the time to kick him or to take revenge because he is no longer an officer over you. That is an evil mindset that will destroy you. Build him up and encourage him: you can come back from this.

precepts.why:
Our profession is this truth. “Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called.” You cannot lay hold on eternal life if you do not hold fast to your profession, and you cannot fight the good fight of faith without holding to it.

Our profession is to go out there, wake up our people, and put in work, because faith without works is dead.

sense.text: This is Christ’s message to us: “For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.” Everything covered is going to be revealed. Some are cooking something up to betray us; we may pretend not to know, but we know.

“Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light.” Whatever you do in darkness is going to come to light. Whatever the backstabbers are playing will come to light. We are not worried, because we have seen the proof over and over again.

The children too live double lives. Check your children’s phones; pour out their school bags; do a deep search. Some sisters got angry when the Bishop warned about it, saying my child would never do that, but the scriptures speak of the heart of a child and how evil it is. When the Bishop, the deacons, captains and officers correct you, it is for your own good, and correction is not always nice: if a child is reaching into the fire, you scream. Put your emotion aside. Is what the Bishop said true? If it is true, the hell with your emotion.

Here is what secret sin costs. “But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing.” Joshua was commanded to go to war, take nothing, and burn everything, and here comes this one man.

Joshua sent men to view Ai, and they came back and said, “Let not all the people go up; but let about two or three thousand men go up and smite Ai.” They had spied the land and thought the city could be taken easily, “for they are but few.”

“They fled before the men of Ai”, and “the men of Ai smote of them about thirty and six men.” Thirty-six Israelites died because of one man; there is always that one negro. The rest of the army ran from a few men, because the Most High was not with Israel that day. “Wherefore the hearts of the people melted, and became as water.”

“Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant.” It was a secret sin: no man saw Achan, but the Most High saw him. “They have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff.” “Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies.”

To find out who committed the sin, Joshua brought Israel by their tribes, setting Judah apart, Benjamin apart, Levi apart. He was investigating: “the tribe of Judah was taken”, then the family of the Zarhites, then Zabdi, then man by man until Achan was taken.

Joshua told him to confess to the Lord: “make confession unto him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me.” Achan confessed he saw “a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them”, and hid them in the earth in his tent.

Israel was in the middle of war, and this man found time to steal. We have brothers like that today, giving up their rank in the middle of warfare. Whatever he wanted could have waited until the war was over. All it takes is one; one bad apple kills everything else.
Joshua sent messengers and they found it all hid in his tent, and laid it out before the Lord. That man was covetous; it was all covetousness.

Joshua took Achan, the silver, the garment, the gold, “and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had.” Why the whole household? Because they had to have known about it. They knew and said nothing, so none of them was innocent. When you see sin or hear of sin, you have to speak up, because silence is agreement.

“Why hast thou troubled us? the Lord shall trouble thee this day.” A lot of you trouble us with your foolishness in the middle of warfare. Some want this teaching to stop; some brothers’ households carry a spirit that troubles the work of Messiah and hinders this truth. Do Messiah a favor and leave; you are taking a seat a brother or sister out there could have used.

“And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones.” We cannot stone you, but we know there is a God who is going to bring judgment, and some will wish they had been stoned instead.

“And they raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day.” That is the result of secret sin: men lost their lives and a whole family was wiped out; none of them was spared. Some do not want to fix their secret sin because in their minds they will never get caught. That is what Satan tells you, and you forgot there is a God.

A second example of the result of secret sin. Ananias and Sapphira “sold a possession, and kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it.” His wife knew. It is impossible for a husband to be doing something illegal and the wife not know. Every woman knows how much her husband makes; she cannot live in a house they cannot afford and pretend she does not know where the money comes from. She knew and did not stop it, because she was living good. When Esau shows up, everybody has to go.

They thought nobody knew. We all think nobody knows: I come here every Sabbath, I am mighty in the scriptures, but during the week nobody knows what I am doing.

“Why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost?” The devil convinced him nobody would know. It is the same spirit then and now: they did not look at the apostles as spiritual men, so they thought Peter would not find out, just as some come to this table and lie in the leaders’ faces, thinking they will not find out.
“Thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.” For the liars, for those fighting homosexuality, for the adulterers, for the thieves: you have not lied unto men, but unto God.

“And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost”: he dropped dead right there. Imagine someone lying at this table and dropping dead, and the negro mind still says, that can never happen to me. You really underestimate Messiah.

“And great fear came on all them that heard these things.” All it takes is one to drop dead, and everyone knows what to do: Bishop, you were right. The Most High knows how the negro thinks; the only thing that can change him is death. If the sister who cheated, or the brother headed to the bar or the hotel, knew they would drop dead the minute they did it, they would not do it.

Three hours later his wife came in, “not knowing what was done.” Peter did not tell her on purpose, to see what she would say: “Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much?” She gave the same answer her husband gave. “How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord?” And she fell down and yielded up the ghost, and was buried by her husband.

Both dropped dead for secret sin. And they did not even have to lie; it was their own land. But they did not look at these men as righteous men, and they did not fear the Most High. We have the same spirit in our midst. The result of secret sin is death.

“For we walk by faith, not by sight.” Faith without works is dead. You cannot just say you have faith and never put in works; faith and works go hand in hand, and by your works we see your faith. Some come every week, listen, and bounce after class without a meaningful conversation with a brother or sister, yet have meaningful conversations with the wicked at the job, at the bar, or on the phone with wicked family. You think you have faith, but you cannot fool us, and you cannot fool the Most High.
“Willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.” Paul understood something about death that many do not.

“Wherefore we labour”: we put in works, “that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him.” The work is not only on the Sabbath. Some soldiers make every Camp 101 and every weeknight class, while some leaders and some with no job never come. Examine yourselves: do you really believe this, and do you really want the kingdom? Some cannot see themselves without America and the white man, spoiled by internet, television, cell phones, lights and food twenty-four seven.

“For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world.” To get the kingdom you must overcome the world. The sins named in this class were not to shame anyone, but so each can examine himself and catch himself; we all want to see each other make it. You must overcome the wickedness of America, and you must overcome yourself, whatever you are fighting.

“And this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.”

“Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God?” Some do not believe that Jesus is the Son of God, so they will never overcome the world. You know they have no faith because the Bishop has been saying prepare, prepare, prepare, and they still say it can never happen here, this is America, not Africa. Now look at what is happening: food sky high, and a president doing what nobody believed one would do. It is going to get worse.
“And because iniquity shall abound”, because sin shall abound, “the love of many shall wax cold.” Look how we kill each other; we are killing our own children.

“But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.” Overcoming is the same thing as enduring to the end. The one who overcomes, who endures to the end, gets the kingdom: your personal sin, your personal trial and tribulation, whatever you are facing, you have to overcome it, and the test is right here in Babylon the Great.

“And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death.” Your children, your wife, your husband may cause you to be put to death.

A sister came into the truth and her husband would not believe, so they went separate ways. One year, two, five, six years passed without her getting a husband in IUIC; she grew desperate and discouraged, with no faith and no patience, and went back to the ex, forgetting he still hated Messiah. Light cannot dwell with darkness. He did not change; he hates Messiah more.

We have seen brothers go to court against their wives, and the judge gave the brother all the kids. And some let their unbelieving children live in their house, having babies out there, because of the wife’s emotion and tears: that is my son, that is my daughter. You allow it because you do not believe. The truth hurts, but it is the truth.

“And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake.” Messiah said we are going to be hated for this truth. “But he that endureth to the end shall be saved.” The scripture keeps repeating itself because we are going to go through these things. Every one of us is going to be tried; it is not if but when. When your time comes, don’t run.

Do not run from the brotherhood. Keep the unity going if you want to put fear in the other nations’ hearts. No matter what, brothers and sisters, do not break the circle; break it, and you give the enemy space to come in.

“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life”: that is the kingdom. But you have to endure. Whatever evil, whatever sin you are in, repent from it and do not do it anymore.

“Which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.” The key word is love him. God is not just going to give you the kingdom. Hate God and you will not get it; hate the brother or sister sitting next to you and you will not get it. Whatever it is, fix it now; tomorrow is promised to none of us.

“Forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before.” Forget the past and let it go; look to what is before you. Some will be destroyed by the past because they refuse to let go of what so-and-so did twenty years ago.

Twenty years ago is twenty atonements past. You went to Messiah at the atonement crying for him to forgive you, yet you still hold a grudge against your brothers and sisters. While you will not forgive that brother or sister, those sins of yours stay. Forget the past and look forward.

“Behold, I come quickly.” No man knows the day or the hour, and tomorrow is promised to none of us. Whatever it is, fix it right now.

“Hold that fast which thou hast.” What we have is enough to get us the kingdom of heaven; hold on to it, brothers and sisters. The kingdom is not based on how many precepts you can break down. If one chapter is the only one you know, or you can break down John 3:16 to the teeth, go out and teach it. Wake up your people. Do something.

“That no man take thy crown.” You worked for it. Do not let any man take your crown.
